`reportError` is used in two places in the patient chart, and both are error-reporting hooks. Each only runs when an error occurs, so a change in `reportError`'s behaviour would show up there, but nothing else in the chart calls it.

**What `reportError` does now.** It normalises the value with `ensureErrorObject` and rethrows it inside `setTimeout`, so the error surfaces as an uncaught global error (`window.onerror`) rather than being handled inline. @file:{github.com/openmrs/openmrs-esm-core::packages/framework/esm-error-handling/src/index.ts:56-61}

**Chart call sites, most affected first:**

1. **`useOrderableConceptSWR`** calls `reportError(error)` in a `useEffect` whenever the SWR fetch fails. It has no dependency array, so it runs on every render while `error` is set. @file:{github.com/openmrs/openmrs-esm-patient-chart::packages/esm-patient-common-lib/src/orders/useOrderableConceptSets.ts:23-61}, call at line 36.

2. **`useOrderableConceptSets`** is the public hook built on that SWR call. It calls `reportError(error)` in a second `useEffect` keyed on `[error]`. @file:{github.com/openmrs/openmrs-esm-patient-chart::packages/esm-patient-common-lib/src/orders/useOrderableConceptSets.ts:65-91}, call at line 73. It is the hook the orders UI consumes, so it is the main place where a change would reach users.

3. **`useFavoritesActions` → `persistFavorites`** calls `reportError(error)` in the `catch` block when saving drug favourites fails, then shows an error snackbar. @file:{github.com/openmrs/openmrs-esm-patient-chart::packages/esm-patient-orders-app/src/order-favorites/useFavoritesActions.ts:18-108}, with the call at line 57 inside `persistFavorites` at @file:{github.com/openmrs/openmrs-esm-patient-chart::packages/esm-patient-orders-app/src/order-favorites/useFavoritesActions.ts:25-68}.

**Mocks.** The framework's own test mocks also declare `reportError` (for example @file:{github.com/openmrs/openmrs-esm-core::packages/framework/esm-framework/mock.tsx:52-55} and @file:{github.com/openmrs/openmrs-esm-core::packages/framework/esm-framework/mock-jest.tsx:51-54}). If the signature or semantics change, these would need matching updates for chart tests that rely on them, but they are not runtime code.

**Limits.** The chart grep and the symbol-reference lookup both returned the same two files, so I found no other direct uses. I did not check whether `reportError` is re-exported through `@openmrs/esm-framework` in a way that would hide a call, and I did not check the other 40+ OpenMRS repositories. I also did not look at whether the chart's tests assert on `reportError` calls beyond the mock definitions.
